messages:
maya.chen: quick follow-up from the fused-attention RFC review — found a parity gap when we enable the dropout-free inference path + QKV fusion on int8. small reproducer shows token-level divergence after ~20 tokens. anyone seen this?
kevin: I was poking at something similar last week. is it only with bias+rope fused or with plain fused-qkv too?
sasha: curious — can you paste the minimal repro / config? might be quantization rounding or the rope application order.
maya.chen: repro below (trimmed):
```
# model config
fusion: enabled
quant: int8
dropout_infer: true
qkv_layout: fused
rope_mode: in-kernel
```
observed: samplers diverge between fused path and baseline after 16-24 tokens. deterministic seed, same prompt.
kevin: thanks. two quick guesses: 1) we apply rotary before adding q/bias in one kernel and after in the other, 2) fast path uses approximate matmul kernel (FP16 accumulation) vs baseline FP32.
liam: can you run with `ACCUMULATE_FP32=true` in the kernel env? that will tell us accumulation precision impact.
maya.chen: ran that — with FP32 accumulation divergence disappears. so it's numeric precision.
sasha: ok that means we need to standardize accumulation or accept small drift. For int8 we do per-channel scales — are we using asymmetric vs symmetric?
kevin: current quant pipeline uses asymmetric scales for weights and symmetric for activations. that mismatch can produce bias when combined with fused bias add + rope multiply in low precision.
liam: two operational options: 1) change kernel to use FP32 accumulation for fused qkv when quantized (costly), 2) add a post-fusion correction step (cheap but hacky), 3) fall back to unfused path if we detect int8 + rope_in_kernel + dropoutless.
maya.chen: fallback has the simplest correctness story but hurts perf for that workload. we should quantify how frequent that combination is in telemetry. can someone query prod traces for requests hitting int8+rope_in_kernel? cc @runtime-bot
runtime-bot: querying metrics... found 734k requests in last 7d with quant=int8 and rope_mode=in-kernel. 58% also had dropout_infer=true (likely from models marked for inference-mode). Avg latency delta if fallback: +12ms tail.
sasha: 12ms tail is non-trivial but maybe acceptable if it's rare per model. we could do a routing rule: keep fused path for most, but enforce FP32 accum on the canary group.
kevin: we also need unit tests for kernel equivalence: microbench that compares fused vs unfused logits across long sequences (up to 1024) and random seeds. if drift > eps we fail. I can sketch a harness.
maya.chen: yes add tests. also need to add an explicit kernel contract in the runtime infra: guaranteed order of ops for fused kernels should be documented (q->k->v layout, bias add semantics, rope multiply timing, accumulation precision). otherwise each optimized kernel diverges in unexpected ways.
liam: plus we should expose a knob in the model config `force_fp_accumulation` so customers can opt-in when they need exact parity with baseline. default false for perf.
sasha: rollout plan: 1) add tests + perf measurement (kevin) 2) implement FP32 accumulation toggle (eng-runtime) 3) telemetry rule to detect int8+rope combos and route small % to canary with FP32 accum 4) if failures -> fallback to unfused runtime.
kevin: timeline: I can have test harness + initial perf numbers in 2 days. adding toggle should be small (a runtime env flag + kernel branch).
maya.chen: question on telemetry: do we have per-request model-level quant metadata in traces? runtime-bot said yes, but is that indexed by model+route?
runtime-bot: yes, traces include model_version, quant_format, rope_mode, route_id. retention 30d.
sasha: good. last bit — dropoutless path: some models relied on dropout RNG side-effects to shape logits slightly; removing dropout can change sampling distribution even in fp32. suggest we call it out in docs and the canary checklist.
liam: agree — doc snippet suggestion: "When enabling dropoutless inference, expect potential small distributional shifts vs training-time outputs; use eval prompts to guard."
maya.chen: cool. I'll open a follow-up PR with the kernel contract and a proposed config flag. kevin, can you add the harness issue and link it?
kevin: on it. creating issue now.
kevin: https://redwood.internal/issue/ENG-RT-5342 added — contains harness, perf run steps, and expected thresholds.
maya.chen: thanks. tagging this thread for the RFC follow-up meeting on Friday. :+1:
liam: likewise, can we add a small synthetic perf bench to the canary infra so we detect regressions automatically?
sasha: yes, add a perf job that runs the fused vs unfused microbench nightly and fails on >5% tail regressions.
maya.chen: perfect. moving to action items.
[thread closed]
